docs.title: Home
docs.text:
First session defaults

Serial 115200 → type help. Lab PIN in sketches/future screens: 1234 (change in user_config.h). Details: Default PINs & serial.

No Wi-Fi / no web UI: RP2350 has no radio. There is no 192.168.4.1 Lab Console — control the board from Serial Monitor and USB HID to your PC. For the browser dashboard, use HackCard ESP32.

docs.title: HackCard RP2350
docs.text:
Credit-card sized RP2350 lab board — NFC, USB HID, RGB, buzzer, and a USB serial lab at 115200 baud.

Firmware v0.1.0

docs.title: How to run an example
docs.text:
1. Run scripts/install-library.ps1 once.
  2. Tools → Generic RP2350, 2MB (no FS), USB Stack: Pico SDK.
  3. File → Examples → HackCard RP2350 → pick one sketch.
  4. Edit // EDIT ME at the top (PINs, URLs, enrolled tag UIDs).
  5. Upload one sketch at a time.
  6. Serial Monitor 115200.

docs.text:
• Destructive NFC labs (erase/kill) and lock/unlock sketches require tags and PCs you own or have permission to use.
  • Default lab PIN 1234 if the sketch asks for one — match LAB_MODE_PIN in user_config.h.

docs.title: Flash firmware
docs.text: Upload HackCard_RP2350.ino and verify the serial lab.

docs.title: Before upload
docs.text:
• First setup board settings (Generic RP2350, 2MB (no FS), Pico SDK)
  • Optional: Personalize user_config.h
  • Serial Monitor: 115200, line ending Newline (NL or CR+LF)

docs.title: Upload steps
docs.text:
1. Open HackCard_RP2350/HackCard_RP2350/HackCard_RP2350.ino
  2. Select the correct COM port
  3. Upload
  4. Open Serial Monitor @ 115200
  5. Press RESET if the banner is missing

docs.title: Expected result
docs.text:
Boot text should show board name, firmware 0.1.0, and PN532/SD status. Then a prompt for commands, for example:

hackcard>

Type:

help

You should see a command list (nfc, vcard, sd, hid, …).

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text: Check Pass signal Serial help prints commands NFC nfc with a tag near the antenna prints UID HID hid hello types on this PC after countdown (focus a text field) Button Short press triggers one NFC read in main firmware

docs.title: If upload fails
docs.text: Symptom Try Wrong chip profile 2MB (no FS), not 4 MB HID/Keyboard compile errors USB Stack: Pico SDK No COM port Data cable; hold BOOT while plugging in if needed

docs.title: Install tools & connect USB
docs.text: Prepare Arduino for Generic RP2350 and connect HackCard over USB-C.

docs.title: Step 1 — Connect HackCard
docs.text:
1. USB-C data cable to your PC.
  2. Confirm a COM port appears after drivers install (Windows may need a moment for Pico/RP2350 CDC).

docs.title: Step 2 — Install Arduino IDE
docs.text: Arduino IDE 2.x

docs.title: Step 3 — Install RP2350 board support
docs.text:
Tools → Board → Boards Manager → install:

Raspberry Pi Pico/RP2040/RP2350 by Earle F. Philhower, III (arduino-pico).

docs.title: Step 4 — Install libraries
docs.text:
Tools → Manage Libraries:

Library Purpose Adafruit PN532 NFC Adafruit BusIO PN532 dependency Adafruit NeoPixel RGB strip

Keyboard, Mouse, SD, SPI, Wire ship with the Philhower core.

docs.title: Step 5 — Install HackCard_RP2350 library
docs.text:
From repo root:

cd HackCard_RP2350\scripts
.\install-library.ps1

Restart Arduino IDE. Examples appear under File → Examples → HackCard RP2350.

docs.title: Step 6 — Open firmware sketch
docs.text:
HackCard_RP2350/HackCard_RP2350/HackCard_RP2350.ino

Tools (critical):

Setting Value Board Generic RP2350 Flash Size 2MB (no FS) — W25Q16 on HackCard USB Stack Pico SDK (not Adafruit TinyUSB) CPU Speed 150 MHz (default OK)

Wrong flash size (e.g. 4 MB Pico 2 profile) or wrong USB stack breaks upload or HID.

Full table: ARDUINO_SETUP.md in the firmware tree.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
HackCard RP2350 is the USB-centric sibling of the ESP32-S3 board: same NFC and HID teaching goals, without Wi-Fi, BLE, or a web Lab Console.

You flash firmware with Arduino IDE, then run labs from Serial Monitor @ 115200 (help, nfc, hid, …) while USB HID actions go to the PC the cable is plugged into.

docs.title: What you get in software
docs.text: Piece What it does HackCard_RP2350.ino Serial lab firmware — commands, NFC, HID demos HackCard_RP2350 library 40 standalone Arduino examples Production test sketch Factory QC (sketches/HackCard_Production_Test/)

docs.title: RP2350 vs ESP32-S3
docs.text: RP2350 ESP32-S3 Control UI Serial @ 115200 Lab Console @ http://192.168.4.1/ Wi-Fi / BLE labs No Yes USB HID to PC Yes (Pico SDK USB) Yes (TinyUSB) NFC (PN532) Yes Yes Arduino core Philhower arduino-pico Espressif esp32 User guide RP2350 guide ESP32 guide

docs.title: What HackCard RP2350 is not
docs.text:
• Not a Wi-Fi tool — no scan, AP, or captive portal on this chip.
  • Not an NFC emulator — PN532 is a reader/writer for external tags.
  • Not a hidden keyboard on someone else’s PC without consent — HID only affects the host you plug into.

docs.title: Factory reset (SD lab files)
docs.text:
1. Examples → HackCard RP2350 → 06_System → Factory_Reset
  2. Upload; Serial 115200
  3. Hold user button 3 s or type RESET
  4. Re-upload HackCard_RP2350.ino

Removes /nfc, /ducky, /payloads, /logs, /hackcard on SD — not your user_config.h text until you edit and re-flash.

docs.title: Personalize settings
docs.text:
Edit HackCard_RP2350/config/user_config.h before you share the board.

There is no Wi-Fi AP on RP2350 — identity fields are used for vcard, NDEF examples, and serial status.

docs.title: Identity (contact / vCard)
docs.text:
Define Purpose USER_NAME, USER_TITLE, USER_COMPANY Contact card USER_EMAIL, USER_PHONE Contact fields USER_WEBSITE, USER_LINKEDIN, USER_GITHUB Links USER_BIO Short line

Example:

#define USER_NAME               "Alex Kim"
#define USER_EMAIL              "lab@example.com"
#define USER_WEBSITE            "https://auratechkick.github.io/HackCard/rp2350/"
#define USER_GITHUB             "https://github.com/auratechkick/HackCard"

docs.title: Lab PIN
docs.text:
Define Default Purpose LAB_MODE_PIN 1234 Reserved for lab-style confirmations in firmware/examples

Change before handout

Default 1234 is public in this repo. Set your own PIN before classroom or client use.

There is no AP_PASSWORD on this board (no Wi-Fi).

docs.title: Comfort defaults
docs.text: Define Purpose DEFAULT_RING_BRIGHTNESS 10–100 DEFAULT_BUZZER_VOLUME 10–100 BOOT_ANIMATION Startup animation BUZZER_ENABLED Master buzzer ACTIVITY_LOGGING Activity log when SD allows SD_AUTO_CREATE_FOLDERS Create lab folders on mount

docs.title: After editing
docs.text:
Save and re-upload HackCard_RP2350.ino.

To clear SD lab files (not user_config.h), use example 06_System/Factory_Reset, then flash main firmware again.

docs.title: Serial lab console
docs.text:
The RP2350 interface is USB serial at 115200 baud — not a browser. Think of it as a text Lab Console.

Full command reference in firmware: HackCard_RP2350/docs/SERIAL_CONSOLE.md.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. USB-C to your PC (same cable carries HID to that PC).
  2. Arduino Serial Monitor or any terminal → 115200, newline.
  3. Type help.

docs.title: Essential commands
docs.text:
Command Action help List all commands status MCU, NFC, SD, owner from config nfc Read one tag (UID / type) watch Toggle continuous NFC reads url https://… Write NDEF URL to a tag you own text hello Write NDEF text vcard Write contact from user_config.h sd Mount SD, create lab folders, list root hid hello After ~3 s, type text on this PC os win / os mac / os linux OS profile for shortcuts site https://… Open URL via OS shortcut notes, lock, shot Notepad/notes, lock, screenshot on this PC log Recent activity (and /logs/activity.log if SD present) rgb idle\|scan\|ok\|err\|off Ring pattern beep Buzzer chime

HID targets your PC

hid, lock, site, etc. only affect the computer HackCard is plugged into. Use your own machine and stay in focus during countdowns.

docs.title: User button (main firmware)
docs.text:
Gesture Typical action Short One NFC read Long Success tone + green ring Double LEDs off

BOOT and RUN are hardware reset/boot — not used as lab GPIO.

docs.title: On-board components
docs.text: Component Detail MCU RP2350 Flash 2 MB external (Arduino: 2MB (no FS)) NFC PN532 + PCB antenna (I2C) RGB WS2812 strip (board-specific pin in HackCard_Pins.h) Buzzer Piezo microSD SPI (optional — lab folders, logs, Ducky scripts) USB-C Power, USB CDC serial, USB HID User button Short / long / double gestures in firmware BOOT / RUN Hardware only — not GPIO-tested in firmware

No SD SD mounted Serial lab help, nfc, basic HID Yes Yes /logs/activity.log, export folders Limited Full layout (/hackcard, /nfc, /payloads, /logs, /ducky) Factory reset example Clears SD lab trees Clears SD lab trees

docs.title: Write your own sketch
docs.text:
Two paths on RP2350:

  1. Serial lab firmware — HackCard_RP2350.ino + terminal commands (help, nfc, …).
  2. Custom example — #include <HackCardRP2350.h> (or library header used in examples) and upload a single-purpose sketch.

docs.title: Start from the template
docs.text:
00_Start_Here/Template_Custom_App

Typical setup:

#include <HackCardRP2350.h>

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  // RgbStrip.begin(...), Buzzer, Buttons, Nfc.begin(), etc.
}

void loop() {
  // Your logic
}

Include only the drivers you need.

docs.title: USB HID notes
docs.text:
• USB Stack: Pico SDK in Arduino Tools (required for Keyboard/Mouse in core).
  • HID output goes to the USB host — the PC connected by USB-C.
  • For Ducky-style payloads, see HID_Ducky_Scripts and /ducky on SD.

Developer guide: CUSTOM_DEVELOPMENT.md

docs.title: When to use ESP32 instead
docs.text: Need Board Browser Lab Console, Wi-Fi, BLE ESP32-S3 — ESP32 guide USB-only classroom, smaller core RP2350 (this guide)

docs.title: Learning path
docs.text:
1. Flash HackCard_RP2350.ino, run help (Serial lab).
  2. Upload one sketch per folder from 01_Board through 03_USB_HID.
  3. Fork Template_Custom_App for your own tool.

Defaults: Default PINs & serial.

docs.title: Authorized use
docs.text: HackCard RP2350 can read/write NFC tags and send USB HID keystrokes to a connected PC.

docs.title: You may use HackCard when
docs.text:
• You own the hardware, tags, and PC, or
  • You have written permission from the owner, or
  • You run a controlled lab or classroom with clear rules.

docs.title: You must not use HackCard to
docs.text:
• Clone or modify access badges or credentials you do not own
  • Run HID or Ducky payloads on machines without the operator’s knowledge
  • Use NFC erase/kill on tags that are not yours or not explicitly designated for lab destruction

docs.title: Before sharing a device
docs.text:
1. Change LAB_MODE_PIN in user_config.h.
  2. Remove enrolled tag UIDs from lock/unlock sketches or re-flash examples with your own policy.
  3. Include an “authorized use only” note.
